title: ClassPass vs Gym Membership in NZ — Which Saves More Money?
meta_desc: Compare ClassPass credit costs with NZ gym membership fees. Find out which option gives you the best value based on real prices and contracts.
intro: Kiwis love flexibility, but does that flexibility come at a higher price? We break down ClassPass credit pricing versus standard gym contracts across New Zealand to see where the real savings lie.

sections.heading: What is ClassPass and how the credit system works
sections.body: ClassPass sells a monthly bundle of credits that you trade for classes, studio time, or specialised sessions. Each activity costs a set number of credits – usually 1 credit for a standard group class, 2‑3 credits for premium or longer workshops. Unused credits roll over for up to three months, giving you a safety net if you miss a week.

sections.heading: Typical New Zealand gym membership rates
When ClassPass gives you the best value
list: You work out 1‑2 times a week and want to sample different studios.
You travel between Auckland, Wellington, and Christchurch and need access to multiple locations.
You prefer boutique classes (e.g., HIIT, Pilates, boxing) that charge extra credits but fit your schedule.
You’re unsure which type of workout you’ll stick with and want to try before committing.

sections.heading: When a dedicated membership wins
list: You hit the gym 4+ times a week – a weekly $15‑$20 membership becomes cheaper than buying credits.
You need 24/7 access to equipment (e.g., weight rooms, cardio machines) that boutique studios don’t always offer.
You prefer a single location with locker rooms, showers, and on‑site personal trainers.
You’re comfortable signing a 12‑month contract to lock in a lower weekly rate.

sections.heading: Bottom line: Which saves more money?
sections.body: If your workout frequency is low or you love hopping between studios, ClassPass can be cheaper – especially with the 30‑credit bundle at $119, which covers up to 15 standard classes a month. However, anyone exercising three or more times a week will see the per‑visit cost drop below $5 with a $15‑$20 weekly gym membership, making a traditional contract the clear winner.
